editorial:
You get a huge, messy, and surprisingly funny look at Napoleon Bonaparte, played by Joaquin Phoenix, as he climbs from soldier to emperor while chasing power and his complicated love for Josephine, played by Vanessa Kirby. The movie mixes big battle scenes with awkward, human moments, so it feels less like a dry history lesson and more like a wild character study. You will see ambition, ego, romance, and bad decisions all packed into one long ride.

The acting is strong, especially Phoenix making Napoleon feel strange and driven, and the war scenes are loud and exciting. The downside is the pacing can drag, and some history feels rushed or skipped. It is long, but the scale and costumes keep you interested. If you like epic dramas with big battles and messy relationships, this is for you.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Napoleon loses at Waterloo and is sent far away to Saint Helena. Josephine has already died, so he is left alone with his memories and writings. He spends his last years in exile, thinking about the empire he lost, and then dies far from France. The movie closes on the sad end of a man who once ruled much of Europe.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves big historical epics and messy love stories.
